title: Card dependencies and ready work
description: Agents need explicit card dependencies to find ready work and work blockers-first; prose references cannot be queried or validated. Keep scope to card-to-card dependencies within one board.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Create and edit dependency links through CLI and UI; expose them through the bridge and direct mode.
Show blockers and dependents on cards and provide a machine-readable way to identify ready work.
Reject invalid, self-referential and cyclic links, including concurrent writes where locking applies.
Define completion, archive and enforcement semantics before implementation.
Preserve existing boards via the documented version upgrade path; update contract, skill and tests including browser coverage.

thread.author: product-manager
thread.body: Should dependencies only inform readiness, or prevent claiming or moving blocked cards into progress? Recommendation: advisory readiness, with no hard workflow enforcement.

thread.author: product-manager
thread.body: When is a dependency satisfied, and what happens if it is archived or missing? Recommendation: only done satisfies it; archived unfinished or missing references remain visible and block readiness.

thread.author: product-manager
thread.body: Product decisions on readiness and enforcement are needed before implementation; recommendations are recorded in the questions.

thread.author: product-manager
thread.body: Independent onboarding feedback from a board with 24 active cards and 4 features: prose dependencies are hard to query. A ready view might also consider status, assignment and open questions; these rules need explicit design rather than assuming every question blocks work. Existing plans require human/agent audit; old checkboxes cannot establish completion.

thread.author: product-manager
thread.body: An independent onboarding report corroborates the need for dependency links; descriptions are the current workaround.
